decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Add / edit / delete bookmarks via a modal dialog', 'URL, title, description, and tags per bookmark — URLs are auto-normalized'. Round 1 client: bare acceptance.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Saving a bookmark by entering a URL is presented and conforms to the reference; no divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Add / edit / delete bookmarks via a modal dialog' with 'URL, title, description, and tags per bookmark'. Round 1 client accepts.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing url/title/description/tags is presented and conforms (note-field editing is out of scope of this presented decision).

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Add / edit / delete bookmarks via a modal dialog'. Round 1 client accepts.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delete is presented and conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'URL, title, description, and tags per bookmark ... tags are deduplicated and lowercased'. Round 1 client accepts.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one or more tags to a bookmark is presented and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Tag sidebar with per-tag counts; click a tag to filter, click "All" to clear'. Round 1 client accepts.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Selecting a tag to filter to that tag's bookmarks is presented and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'renders the seed cards and tag chips'; list exposes title, description, tags, and favicon per item. Round 1 client accepts.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Readability-first list exposing title/description/tags/favicon is presented and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Favicons fetched per site, with graceful fallback' and 'titles default to the site host if left blank', plus future-direction offer 'auto-fetching page titles when you paste a URL' — establishing that only favicons are auto-collected, not page title/description/preview image. Round 1 client: 'I'm happy with the application as it stands' (bare approval, no mention of metadata).
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title, description, favicon, and preview image on save; only favicon is collected, and the maker's own 'future' offer confirms title auto-fetch is absent, so REF-BM-03's editing of auto-collected title/description is unmet in premise. Divergence established independently; client's bare approval surfaces no difference (rubric: bare approval does not qualify), so unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Full-text search across title, description, URL, and tags (live, debounced)'. Round 1 client: 'finding ... my bookmarks' echoed in blanket acceptance.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-12 specifies full-text search over title, description, note, and url; the presented search scope substitutes tags for note (no note field exists), diverging from the reference search targets. Client's approval does not express or contest the difference, so unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered choice: 'A few directions I could take it next if you'd like: importing browser bookmark exports ... Anything in particular you'd want to prioritize?' — establishing Netscape/HTML import is not implemented. Round 1 client: blanket 'happy with the application as it stands' without selecting any offered direction.
decisions.note: Specification/direction gate via offered choice. The offer surfaces that import (REF-BM-30) is absent; the offered alternative fulfils a reference item, but the client neither selected it nor expressed the expectation, so the divergence passes unexpressed (not a select).
